newsitem.title: USA: Prospective jurors now 44 in Miami tobacco case.
newsitem.headline: Prospective jurors now 44 in Miami tobacco case.

text.p: A woman who wept on the witness stand as she remembered relatives who died from smoking- related illnesses was added Tuesday to a pool from which a jury will be picked to hear a landmark $5 billion lawsuit against the cigarette industry.

The woman sobbed openly when a tobacco industry lawyer asked about a statement on her jury questionnaire in which she indicated that family members had "perished" due to cigarette smoking. The woman was accepted into the jury pool despite the emotional outburst and objections from industry lawyers, one of whom told Judge Robert Kaye that, at the very least, the defense was entitled to "a jury that doesn't cry during the trial."

The admission of the woman and six others Monday brought the pool of prospective jurors to 44. Because each of the sides can exclude 27 jurors, a pool of more than 60 will be needed to seat a six-member panel plus alternates.

The lawsuit known as Broin v Philip Morris et al, seeks damages from nine tobacco companies and industry groups on behalf of some 60,000 flight attendants, who say they were made ill by secondhand smoke on U.S.-based passenger jets.
